name: Custom Volume Sampling via GLSL Injection
text:
# Custom Volume Sampling via GLSL Injection

Also called: Custom GLSL Volume Sampling

## Overview
Custom Volume Sampling via GLSL Injection is a mechanism to override the default [volume sampling](#7111-volume-sampling.md) logic by injecting a custom [GLSL](#5184-ray-marching-volume-rendering-glsl.md) function into the fragment shader [S1, unofficial]. This allows arbitrary scalar value calculation at voxel positions and time steps without requiring an atlas texture [S1, unofficial]. It distinguishes itself from standard trilinear sampling by decoupling data retrieval from the texture fetch, enabling dynamic or procedural volume evaluation directly within the rendering pipeline [S1, unofficial].

## How it works
The method intercepts the scalar value retrieval step in the volume ray-marching loop [G]. Instead of performing a `texture3D` (or equivalent) lookup on a bound 3D texture, the renderer executes a custom GLSL function provided by the application [S1, unofficial]. This function computes the density or scalar value based on input parameters, which are passed from the [CPU](#10688-naive-sdf-generation-cpu.md) to the GPU via uniforms [S1, unofficial].

### Inputs and Outputs
*   **Inputs**:
    *   `options.customFunction`: string|null. A custom GLSL function string that overrides the default volume sampling [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.raySteps`: number (default: 64). Number of ray steps for sampling [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.useVolumetricDepthTest`: boolean (default: false). Enables volumetric depth testing [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.useExtinctionCoefficient`: boolean (default: true). Enables extinction coefficient for [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.useValueAsExtinctionCoefficient`: boolean (default: false). Uses the sampled value as the extinction coefficient [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.usePointLights`: boolean (default: false). Enables point lights [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.useDirectionalLights`: boolean (default: false). Enables directional lights [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.useRandomStart`: boolean (default: true). Randomizes ray start position to soften edges [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.renderMeanValue`: boolean (default: false). [Renders the mean](#2070-render-means.md) value across the volume instead of alpha blending [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.invertNormals`: boolean (default: false). Inverts all surface normals [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.renderNormals`: boolean (default: false). Renders surface normals at the first hit [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.minPaletteValue`: number. Minimum value used for palette mapping [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.maxPaletteValue`: number. Maximum value used for palette mapping [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.minCutoffValue`: number. Minimum cutoff value [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.maxCutoffValue`: number. Maximum cutoff value [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.cutoffFadeRange`: number. Range near the cutoff where alpha fades to zero [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.valueMultiplier`: number. Multiplier applied to sampled values [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.valueAdded`: number. Constant added to sampled values after multiplication [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.extinctionCoefficient`: number. Fixed extinction coefficient used for alpha blending [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.extinctionMultiplier`: number. Multiplier applied to the extinction coefficient [S1, unofficial].
    *   `options.alphaMultiplier`: number. Multiplier applied to the final alpha value [S1, unofficial].
    *   `uniforms.normalEpsilon`: number (default: 0.001). Real-unit epsilon used when estimating the forward difference for normals [S1, unofficial].
    *   `uniforms.depthTexture`: Required if `useVolumetricDepthTest` is true [S1, unofficial].
    *   `volumeOrigin`: World-space origin of the volume [G].
    *   `time`: Current time step [S1, unofficial].
*   **Outputs**:
    *   The scalar value returned by the custom function [S1, unofficial].
    *   Final rendered color and alpha based on the accumulated samples and lighting [S1, unofficial].

### Data Structures
The implementation relies on a configuration object `options` passed to the renderer's material update routine [S1, unofficial]. The core data structure for the custom function is a string containing valid GLSL code [S1, unofficial]. The GLSL function signature is fixed:

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```glsl
float sampleValue(float x, float y, float z, float t)
```

Where:
*   `x`, `y`, `z`: Local positions inside the volume in world-space units relative to `volumeOrigin` [S1, unofficial].
*   `t`: The current time [S1, unofficial].
*   Return value: The scalar value at that point [S1, unofficial].

### Parameters and Typical Values
*   `raySteps`: Default 64. Performance scales linearly with this value [S1, unofficial].
*   `useRandomStart`: Default true. Randomizes ray start position to soften edges [S1, unofficial].
*   `useExtinctionCoefficient`: Default true [S1, unofficial].
*   `useValueAsExtinctionCoefficient`: Default false [S1, unofficial].
*   `usePointLights`: Default false. Enables point lights; normals are estimated, decreasing performance [S1, unofficial].
*   `useDirectionalLights`: Default false. Enables directional lights; normals are estimated, decreasing performance [S1, unofficial].
*   `renderMeanValue`: Default false. Renders the mean value across the volume instead of alpha blending [S1, unofficial].
*   `renderNormals`: Default false. Renders surface normals at the first hit; normals are estimated, decreasing performance [S1, unofficial].
*   `normalEpsilon`: Default 0.001. Real-unit epsilon used when estimating the forward difference for normals [S1, unofficial].

### Steps
1.  **Configuration**: The user provides `options.customFunction` as a GLSL string [S1, unofficial].
2.  **Shader Injection**: The renderer injects the `sampleValue` function body into the fragment shader [S1, unofficial].
3.  **Uniform Update**: The renderer updates material uniforms based on `options` [S1, unofficial].
4.  **[Ray Marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) Loop**: For each pixel, a ray is cast through the volume [G]. The loop iterates `raySteps` times [S1, unofficial]. If `useRandomStart` is true, the initial ray origin is perturbed [S1, unofficial]. At each step, the current position `(x, y, z)` relative to `volumeOrigin` and the time `t` are passed to the injected `sampleValue` function [S1, unofficial]. The returned scalar value is processed according to other options [S1, unofficial]. If `renderNormals` is true, normals are estimated using `normalEpsilon` for forward differences, and the shader renders surface normals at the first hit [S1, unofficial]. If `renderMeanValue` is false, cutoffs (`minCutoffValue`, `maxCutoffValue`) are applied [S1, unofficial]. The value is scaled by `valueMultiplier` and offset by `valueAdded` [S1, unofficial]. If `useExtinctionCoefficient` is true and `useValueAsExtinctionCoefficient` is false, the fixed `extinctionCoefficient` (scaled by `extinctionMultiplier`) is used for alpha blending [S1, unofficial]. If `useValueAsExtinctionCoefficient` is true, the sampled value itself acts as the extinction coefficient [S1, unofficial]. If `usePointLights` or `useDirectionalLights` is true, lighting calculations are performed using the estimated normals [S1, unofficial]. The result is accumulated into the final color and alpha, scaled by `alphaMultiplier` if `renderNormals` is false [S1, unofficial].
5.  **Volumetric Depth Test**: If `useVolumetricDepthTest` is true, the renderer expects a `uniforms.depthTexture` to be set and performs depth testing against it [S1, unofficial].

### Pseudocode
The following pseudocode illustrates the injection and execution logic in a Python-like style, representing the CPU-side setup and the resulting GPU-side shader logic. The ray marching loop is handled by the parent renderer [G].

> **Unverified code.** The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors.

```python
def setup_custom_volume_sampling(renderer, options):
    """
    Configures the volume renderer with custom GLSL sampling.
    """
    glsl_code = options.get('customFunction', '')
    signature = "float sampleValue(float x, float y, float z, float t)"
    full_function = f"{signature} {{\n    {glsl_code}\n}}"
    renderer.update_material({
        'custom_function_source': full_function,
        'ray_steps': options.get('raySteps', 64),
        'use_volumetric_depth_test': options.get('useVolumetricDepthTest', False),
        'use_extinction_coefficient': options.get('useExtinctionCoefficient', True),
        'use_value_as_extinction_coefficient': options.get('useValueAsExtinctionCoefficient', False),
        'use_point_lights': options.get('usePointLights', False),
        'use_directional_lights': options.get('useDirectionalLights', False),
        'use_random_start': options.get('useRandomStart', True),
        'render_mean_value': options.get('renderMeanValue', False),
        'invert_normals': options.get('invertNormals', False),
        'render_normals': options.get('renderNormals', False),
        'min_palette_value': options.get('minPaletteValue', 0.0),
        'max_palette_value': options.get('maxPaletteValue', 1.0),
        'min_cutoff_value': options.get('minCutoffValue', 0.0),
        'max_cutoff_value': options.get('maxCutoffValue', 1.0),
        'cutoff_fade_range': options.get('cutoffFadeRange', 0.0),
        'value_multiplier': options.get('valueMultiplier', 1.0),
        'value_added': options.get('valueAdded', 0.0),
        'extinction_coefficient': options.get('extinctionCoefficient', 1.0),
        'extinction_multiplier': options.get('extinctionMultiplier', 1.0),
        'alpha_multiplier': options.get('alphaMultiplier', 1.0),
        'normal_epsilon': renderer.uniforms.normalEpsilon.value
    })

def simulate_gpu_sampling_step(options, position, time, volume_origin):
    """
    Simulates the logic performed in the GPU fragment shader for a single sample.
    """
    # Calculate local position relative to volume origin
    x = position.x - volume_origin.x
    y = position.y - volume_origin.y
    z = position.z - volume_origin.z
    t = time

    # Call the injected custom function
    # The renderer injects the user's GLSL code here [S1, unofficial]
    scalar = injected_sample_value(x, y, z, t)

    # Apply value transformations
    scalar = scalar * options['value_multiplier'] + options['value_added']

    # Handle cutoffs (only if not rendering mean value)
    if not options['render_mean_value']:
        if scalar < options['min_cutoff_value']:
            scalar = 0.0
        elif scalar > options['max_cutoff_value']:
            scalar = 0.0
        else:
            # Fade near cutoffs using cutoffFadeRange
            # Implementation detail: specific fade logic depends on renderer
            pass

    # Handle extinction
    if options['use_extinction_coefficient']:
        if options['use_value_as_extinction_coefficient']:
            extinction = scalar * options['extinction_multiplier']
        else:
            extinction = options['extinction_coefficient'] * options['extinction_multiplier']
    else:
        extinction = 1.0

    # Handle lighting (if enabled)
    color = 0.0
    if options['use_point_lights'] or options['use_directional_lights']:
        # Estimate normal at (x,y,z) using normal_epsilon
        # normal = estimate_normal(x, y, z, options['normal_epsilon'])
        # if options['invert_normals']:
        #     normal = -normal
        # color = apply_lighting(normal, position, time)
        pass

    # Handle rendering mode
    if options['render_normals']:
        # Render normals at first hit
        pass
    elif options['render_mean_value']:
        # Accumulate mean value
        pass
    else:
        # Alpha blending
        # alpha = 1.0 - exp(-extinction * step_size)
        # final_color = accumulate(color, alpha) * options['alpha_multiplier']
        pass

    return scalar, color
```

### Edge Cases and Pitfalls
*   **Performance**: Enabling `usePointLights`, `useDirectionalLights`, or `renderNormals` requires normal estimation via finite differences, which significantly decreases performance [S1, unofficial].
*   **Precision**: The `normalEpsilon` value must be chosen carefully; too small leads to numerical noise, too large leads to inaccurate normals [S1, unofficial].
*   **Boundary Conditions**: The `sampleValue` function must handle coordinates outside the volume bounds gracefully, typically by returning 0 or a background value, as the renderer does not automatically clamp coordinates before passing them to the custom function [G].
*   **Shader Compilation**: Invalid GLSL syntax in `customFunction` will cause shader compilation failure, resulting in a black or error-colored render [G].
*   **Depth Testing**: If `useVolumetricDepthTest` is true but `uniforms.depthTexture` is not set, the depth test will fail or produce undefined results [S1, unofficial].

## Operating characteristics
*   **Time Complexity**: Linear with respect to `raySteps` [S1, unofficial]. Each step involves a call to the custom function and potential lighting/normal calculations [G].
*   **Memory Complexity**: Low. The custom function is stored as a string in the options object [S1, unofficial].
*   **Performance**: Base performance is determined by `raySteps` and the complexity of the custom GLSL function [G]. Enabling lighting or normals adds overhead due to normal estimation [S1, unofficial]. Performance scales linearly with `raySteps` [S1, unofficial].
*   **Strengths**: Flexibility allows arbitrary scalar field definitions, including [procedural noise](#1799-procedural-noise-functions.md), external data lookups, or time-varying fields [G]. No atlas texture is required [S1, unofficial].
*   **Limitations**: GLSL code injection makes debugging harder compared to standard texture sampling [G]. Complex custom functions can be slower than optimized texture lookups [G]. Estimated normals are computationally expensive [S1, unofficial].
*   **When to Use**: When the volume data is dynamic, procedural, or sourced from external systems not easily represented as a 3D texture [G]. When standard trilinear sampling is insufficient for the required scalar field behavior [G].
*   **When Not to Use**: When static, pre-computed volume data is available and performance is critical [G]. When high-quality normals are required without the performance cost of estimation [G].

## Background
Custom Volume Sampling via GLSL Injection is a feature of the `three.js-volume-renderer` library, an unofficial extension for Three.js [S1, unofficial]. It was developed to provide greater flexibility in volume rendering by allowing users to define custom sampling logic directly in the shader, bypassing the need for traditional 3D texture lookups [S1, unofficial]. This approach is particularly useful for real-time applications where volume data is generated procedurally or updated frequently [G].
